Undermine

/un-der-MYN/ - rhymes with shine · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Undermine means to weaken something gradually, especially in an indirect or hidden way.

Season after season, burrowing rabbits undermined the garden wall until one hard frost finally toppled it.

Worked Example

Every time the substitute overruled the seating chart 'just for today,' she undermined it a little more; by June the chart was a suggestion nobody could enforce.

Weaken and damage describe the result; undermine describes the method — from beneath, unseen, a little at a time. What is undermined looks fine on the surface, right up until it suddenly doesn't.

How Strong Is It? — dent → undermine → demolish

dent vs. undermine

dent vs. undermine: A dent is much milder than undermining — visible surface damage that leaves the structure's strength intact.

demolish vs. undermine

demolish vs. undermine: Demolishing goes even further than undermining — an undermined thing still stands, weakened and waiting, while a demolished one is already down.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — under-

Prefix — under-: beneath, below

Root — mine

Root — mine: to dig, to tunnel

Put it together

Put it together: Under- (beneath) + mine (to dig) = to dig beneath. Medieval siege engineers couldn't knock down a castle wall, so they tunneled under it and burned the props; the wall collapsed under its own weight. Every figurative use keeps that blueprint: attack the support, not the surface, and let gravity finish the job.

Use the root in a new word: miner

Use the root in a new word: miner: Her great-grandfather worked as a miner, digging coal from tunnels a hundred meters below the valley floor.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Undermine is the everyday word for hidden, gradual weakening — of walls, confidence, authority, or rules. Use 'erode' when the wearing is natural and impersonal, and 'sap' when strength is being drained from inside. Its unit-mate subvert is narrower and more political: systems and institutions are subverted, but almost anything can be undermined.
